# dsh-semantic-drift
**English** · 简体中文

A DSH plugin that keeps **one versioned vocabulary** of a project's business
concepts, shows where t

he code spells them differently, and gives a person and an
agent a place to decide which spelling is

lls them differently, and gives a person and an
agent a place to decide which spelling is canonical.
DSH shows the plugin as **Semantic Drift Vocabulary** (语义漂移词表).

## Where it comes from

The idea is borrowed from
kurapica/schema-node-csharp,
which argues three things this plugin takes a

is borrowed from
kurapica/schema-node-csharp,
which argues three things this plugin takes as given:

1. **Semantics deserve to be an independent, versioned artifact** — not something
re-derived from th

e code on every read.
2. **A small, enumerable vocabulary** is easier to keep correct than an open-e

nded
type system.
3. **Drift has to be observable and adjudicable**, not something a team is expecte

em.
3. **Drift has to be observable and adjudicable**, not something a team is expected
to remember.

No implementation is borrowed. There is no Meta/Property/Relation model, no semantic
compilation, no

code generation. One YAML file, one read-only scanner, one panel,
five agent tools.
## What it does

**It records what things are called.** Each concept gets one entry: a dotted id,
the human terms for

it, a kind, the canonical symbol (plus type and unit when they
matter) and a note. The file is vers

ioned with the project, so a rename is a diff
someone can review.

**It finds where the code disagrees.** A read-only scan compares the tree with the
vocabulary and re

inds where the code disagrees.** A read-only scan compares the tree with the
vocabulary and reports:

- the same type declared twice — with the member *values* compared, not just names;
- two copies tha

t have diverged (missing members, extra members, swapped enum values);
- a copy that is really a par

ameterized derivative, which must not be merged;
- a spelling variant of a canonical name, including

It works from an empty vocabulary too: the structural detectors compare code with
code, so a fresh p
roject has findings before its first concept exists.

**It gives the decision a home.** An accepted exception carries a reason and the
smallest scope that

covers the case. It can be edited, reworded, removed or undone
later, and each one reports how many

findings it actually mutes right now. The
decision is a line in the vocabulary file, not a memory i

ally mutes right now. The
decision is a line in the vocabulary file, not a memory in someone's head.

**It puts the vocabulary in front of the agent.** Every session receives one prompt
section with the

concepts of the workspace it runs in, plus the rules: look the
concept up before naming something,

spell it exactly as the canonical symbol does,
register a missing concept first, record a deliberate

deviation with a reason. Five
tools let the agent read, register, scan and adjudicate.

**It costs tokens, and you can turn that off.** The prompt section is the recurring
cost; the panel'

s settings switch disables it per profile, and the scan itself costs
nothing until someone asks for
it. Numbers are in Token cost.
## What it does not do

- **It is lexical, not semantic.** It compares identifiers, member names and comment
text. Two unrel

ated types that share a name can still be reported.
- **It does not enforce anything.** The prompt r

ules are advice. An agent can
deviate, and the only defence is that the deviation must be recorded.

- **It does not fix code.** No auto-rename, no auto-merge, no patch. The scan is
trusted precisely b

ecause it never writes your source.
- **Structural detection covers three languages** — C#, TypeScri

pt and Python
declarations. Other files contribute comment/string evidence only.
- **Units are store

d, not checked.** `canonical.unit` is displayed and validated as
a string; there is no unit-drift de

tector.
- **One workspace, one vocabulary.** No cross-repository view.
- **It never decides for you*

* whether the vocabulary file is committed. That is a
project decision; if you commit it, the team s
hares and reviews it.

There is no in-plugin updater: DSH replaces an installed bundle when it is installed
again.

Restart DSH afterwards, then read the version in the panel footer (`vX.Y.Z`) or at

ift/health`; the settings dialog no longer repeats it. An update never
touches your vocabulary file
or its accepted exceptions.
## Getting started

1. Open **Semantic Drift Vocabulary** in a workspace.
2. Press **Create vocabulary** — writes `.dsh/

semantics.yaml` with the default
exclusions and no concepts.
3. Press **Scan**. With no concepts yet

you still get structural findings ("the same
type is defined twice"), which is the cold-start value

.
4. Register a concept with **New concept** (or `semantic_upsert`) and scan again.
Vocabulary-depen

dent findings now have something to compare against.
5. Accept a finding you intend to keep: choose

the **scope** (this file, every
directory with the same file name, the whole symbol, or a custom glo
